note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: On a new factory installation, what is the main difference between pre-commissioning and commissioning?
options: Pre-commissioning is the paperwork, and commissioning is all the hands-on work on site
Pre-commissioning is dead checks; commissioning proves it works with power on
Pre-commissioning is done by the client, and commissioning is done by the contractor's team
Pre-commissioning comes after handover, and commissioning is done before the handover

questions.stem: Which set of headings belongs in a commissioning plan for a new hotel wing?
options: Scope, sequence, roles, tests and acceptance criteria, records, and programme
Cable prices, supplier names, delivery dates and the GCT on each invoice
Staff wages, overtime rates, leave dates and the payroll deductions
Room rates, guest numbers, booking dates and the opening party plan

questions.stem: On a large job, what is the main duty of the commissioning manager?
options: To wire the final circuits faster himself so that the whole team finishes on time
To buy all the test instruments and keep them locked away
To plan, coordinate and record commissioning, and confirm acceptance
To work out the cable sizes and choose every protective device in the design

questions.stem: When a contractor fits out a hotel, what does its inspection and test plan (ITP) list?
options: Where each light fitting is placed in the ceilings of the guest rooms
The price of each test the contractor will charge the hotel for at the end
Which instruments are kept in the van, with their serial numbers and owners
Each check and test, when it is done, who does it, and the accepted result

questions.stem: On the ITP for a new sub-board, one step is marked as a 'hold point'. What does that tell the team?
options: Work stops at that step until the named person checks and releases it
The team may carry on with the work if the client's engineer does not arrive
The place where the tester's probe is held on the terminal to take a reading
A break in the working day when the team rests and the site is left locked up

questions.stem: In an ITP, what does a 'witness point' mean?
options: The work must stop for good until a dispute between the client and contractor is settled
The named person is told in time and may attend; if not, work goes on
Only the client is allowed to carry out that test, never the contractor or the maker
The test is skipped altogether if a witness from another trade is not on site that day

questions.stem: Before a new distribution board is energised for the first time, which records must be complete and checked?
options: The delivery notes for the board and the cable drums
The inspection and dead test results for the board and its circuits
The daily site diary and the list of workers' phone numbers
The receipts for the breakers and the board's paint colour code

questions.stem: A new building has a main board, three sub-boards and many final circuits. In what order is it energised?
options: The final circuits first, then the sub-boards, and the main board last of all
All the boards at the same moment, so that the whole building comes on together
From the supply outward: main board, sub-boards, then final circuits
The sub-boards first, in any order, then the main board, then the final circuits

questions.stem: Why are all the outgoing breakers on a new board switched off before its incoming supply is first switched on?
options: So that the meter does not record the energy used while testing is being done
So the board's paint and labels are not damaged by the heat of the first current
So each circuit can be switched on and checked one at a time
So the breakers do not wear out before the client finally takes the building over

questions.stem: Part of a new office block is now live, but other trades still work there. What must the commissioning manager arrange?
options: Live notices, barriers or locked rooms, and a briefing to every trade
Faster working, so that all the other trades finish before the power comes on
A sign at the main gate only, since the trades can see which lights are working
Nothing extra, because only the electricians ever open the distribution boards

questions.stem: Why is a marked-up drawing showing which boards and cables are now live kept on the site office wall during commissioning?
options: It tells the client how much energy each board will use in a month
Everyone can see at once what is energised before they plan any work
It replaces the need for locks and tags on the boards that are still dead
It shows the painters which walls are ready for their first coat

questions.stem: After a sub-board has been energised, a fault is found on one of its circuits. How should work on that circuit now be controlled?
options: Any electrician may work on it if they wear rubber gloves
The trainee who wired it fixes it while the board stays on
It is left until handover so the programme is not delayed
Under a permit to work, with isolation, lock-off and proving dead

questions.stem: How is a mains failure normally simulated to test a generator's automatic transfer switch (ATS)?
options: An authorised person opens the mains incoming breaker, as agreed
A trainee pulls out the transfer switch control wires while the generator is running
The power company cuts the street supply to the whole area
The generator's fuel valve is closed to see whether the mains will take over the load

questions.stem: When the mains returns after a generator test, why does the ATS wait for a set time before it switches the load back?
options: To let the generator's fuel tank fill up again from the day tank before it stops
To be sure the mains is steady and has not just flickered back
To give the client time to pay for all the fuel that was used during the test
To let the power company's meter reader record the reading before the switch-over

questions.stem: Why is a new standby generator often tested with a load bank during commissioning?
options: To clean out the radiator by blowing hot air through its fins for an hour
To charge the starting battery faster than its own battery charger can do
To prove it carries its full rated load steadily for the time specified
To check the paint finish under heat before the maker's warranty period starts

questions.stem: A new three-phase extract fan motor is to be checked for direction of rotation. Which method is best?
options: Run it at full load for an hour and listen carefully for any strange noise
Ask the plumber which way the pipes are laid and work out the direction from that
Check the colours of the cable cores at the motor's terminal box against the drawing
A brief start by an authorised person, watching the shaft or fan blades

questions.stem: A motor's nameplate gives a full-load current of 14.2 A. The overload relay has a dial from 10 A to 16 A. Unless the maker says otherwise, where is it set?
options: 16 A, the top of the dial
10 A, the bottom of the dial
14.2 A, the full-load current
28.4 A, twice the full-load current

questions.stem: During commissioning of a hotel, the fire alarm interface is tested. Which result shows the interface works?
options: The fire alarm panel shows the time and date correctly
The air handling units shut down and the held-open fire doors close
The guest room lights all switch on at full brightness
The kitchen extract fans speed up to clear the smoke

questions.stem: How is a new emergency lighting system proved at commissioning?
options: Cut the normal supply; the fittings must stay lit for their full rated time
Take out each lamp and check it with a continuity tester at the bench in the workshop
Switch the fittings on and off at the wall switch five times and watch each one
Weigh each battery to confirm that it is fully charged before the client moves in

questions.stem: A new three-phase sub-board has just been energised by the authorised person. Which readings are taken first?
options: The insulation resistance of each circuit at 500 V
The voltages at the board and the phase rotation
The continuity of each protective conductor
The resistance of the earth electrode at the main board

questions.stem: Once the building is on load, the phase currents on a sub-main read 62 A, 48 A and 70 A. The average is 60 A. What is the largest difference from the average, as a percentage of it?
Why is a thermal imaging survey of the main board done after the building has been on load for some hours, not at the moment it is switched on?
options: Joints heat up only after current has flowed a while, so loose ones show then
The camera works properly only when the board is standing in full direct sunlight
The power company asks for all the thermal photographs to be taken at night only
The camera's battery needs several hours to warm up before it gives any readings

questions.stem: Which item belongs on a snag (punch) list at the end of a job?
options: A light switch plate fitted crooked in an office
The name of a worker who was late on Monday
The price of the cable used on the second floor
The date the next project starts in Negril

questions.stem: A snag list has two kinds of item: those that stop handover and those that can be cleared later. Which item must be cleared before handover?
options: A scratched cover plate in a store room
A missing circuit label on a spare way
An emergency light that goes out after ten minutes
A cable tie left uncut in the ceiling void

questions.stem: During commissioning, which event calls for a non-conformance report (NCR)?
options: Each morning, to record who is on site that day
When a delivery arrives early and must be stored
When the client asks for a copy of the programme
When a test result or item does not meet the specification

questions.stem: During a witness test, the generator fails to pick up the load in the time the specification allows. What should happen?
options: Record the failure, fix the cause, then retest with the witness there
Change the result on the test sheet so that it matches the specification time
Pass it anyway, because the generator did start up and take the load in the end
Skip it and test the next system, then hand the building over as was planned

questions.stem: Why is each instrument's serial number and calibration date written on the commissioning test sheets?
options: So the instruments can be sold later on at a better price to another firm
So readings can be traced to an instrument known to be accurate
So the client can see which brand of instrument the contractor likes best
So the store keeper knows which member of the team borrowed each instrument

questions.stem: Which details should every commissioning test sheet carry?
options: The tester's home address, phone number and next of kin in case of accident
The weather that day and the other trades on site
Item, date, instrument, readings, accepted limits and signatures
The price charged for each test and the date that it will be invoiced to the client

questions.stem: A new UPS is to be commissioned. Why is the maker's engineer often asked to attend?
options: The maker's set-up and checks may be needed to keep the warranty valid
The maker's engineer is the only person allowed to sign the snag list
The maker's engineer must pay for the batteries if they fail
The maker's engineer replaces the government inspector on site

questions.stem: Why should the project programme allow a separate block of time for commissioning before the handover date?
options: So the whole team can take their leave before the client moves into the building
Testing, finding and fixing faults, and then retesting all take real time
So the client still has time to change the design at the very last moment
So the materials left over can be counted, packed and sold before the team leaves

questions.stem: Why is training the client's maintenance staff part of commissioning?
options: It lets the contractor charge for extra hours after the job
It means the contractor need not provide an O&M manual
It is only needed when the staff are new to the company
So they can run, isolate and look after the systems safely

questions.stem: What does an operation and maintenance (O&M) manual give the client?
options: The contractor's prices for any future work that is done in the building
How each system works and is looked after, with spares and test records
The list of every worker on the job and the hours that each of them spent
The planning permission for the building and the land title for the site

questions.stem: During the job, several cable routes were changed from the design. What must happen to the drawings before handover?
options: Updated to as-built drawings showing what was really installed
Kept exactly as designed, because the changes made on site were only small ones
Thrown away, since nobody will need them again
Given to the power company in place of the inspection and test results

questions.stem: What does 'practical completion' (handover) mean on an installation contract?
options: Every possible defect has been found and fixed, and the contract is fully closed
The client has paid every bill, including the retention money held back
The work is finished and safe to use, with only small items left
The contractor's team has left and the gate is locked

questions.stem: What is the 'defects liability period' after handover?
options: A time when the client may not use the building at all
A set time when the contractor must put right defects that appear
The time the contractor has to send the final invoice
The time the government inspector has to visit the site

questions.stem: A new commercial building in Portmore is ready. Which step must come before the power company connects its supply?
options: The client opens the shop to customers for a trial week
The contractor's own team signs a letter of completion
The other trades sign that their work is finished
The government electrical inspection and its certificate

questions.stem: When commissioning a grid-tied solar PV inverter, why is its anti-islanding function checked?
options: It stops sending power out when the grid fails, to protect line workers
It keeps the whole building lit from the panels when the grid fails at night
It turns the solar panels to face the sun as it moves across the sky each day
It sends more power out to the grid during the hottest part of the afternoon

questions.stem: A client wants a new grid-tied PV system to send power into the grid. What must the commissioning plan include?
options: A note that the panels need washing once a year
The power company's approval and checks before export starts
A check that the inverter's display shows the correct date and time of day
Painting the inverter cabinet to match the colour of the rest of the building

questions.stem: What does a UPS battery autonomy test prove?
options: The batteries are the right colour and size for the cabinet
The UPS fan runs quietly enough for an office
The UPS display shows the right language and time
The UPS carries its load on batteries for the time specified

questions.stem: A power factor correction capacitor bank has been isolated for a check. Before touching it, what must be done?
options: Touch the terminals quickly with the back of the hand
Switch it off and on again three times to drain it
Wait the discharge time the maker marks, then prove dead
Spray it with water to cool it before working

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a short daily commissioning meeting on a busy site?
options: To agree the day's tests, shutdowns, access and who does what
To share out the overtime fairly between the trades
To read the full specification aloud to every worker
To sign off the project and release the retention money

questions.stem: Commissioning a new sub-board in a busy supermarket needs a short shutdown of the freezers. What is the best plan?
options: Do it at the busiest time of day so the staff are there to help move stock
Do it without warning, as it takes only minutes
Agree an out-of-hours time and plan cover for the freezer stock
Leave the freezers running and connect the new board while it is still live

questions.stem: A keen trainee on your commissioning team asks to switch on the new main board. What should you tell him?
options: Yes, as long as he wears insulated gloves and safety goggles
Yes, as long as the client is standing nearby to watch him
No: only the authorised person switches on, as agreed
Yes, but only after lunch, when the site is quieter

questions.stem: Why are the actual readings written on commissioning sheets, not just the word 'pass'?
options: Readings take less time to write than words
The client is not allowed to see the word 'pass'
Readings make the sheets look longer and more complete
Later tests can be compared with them to spot changes

questions.stem: Twelve sub-boards must be commissioned. Each takes 3 hours, and the team works 7.5 hours a day on them. How many working days should be planned?
options: 3 days
4 days
5 days
6 days

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the list of small defects and unfinished items, to be closed out before or after handover, usually called?
What is the report called that is raised when an item or test result does not meet the specification? (words or letters)
In an inspection and test plan, what is the step called where work must stop until a named person inspects and releases it?
What is the device called that changes a building's load from the mains to a standby generator by itself when the mains fails? (words or letters)
What is the test called in which a generator runs a bank of resistors or other artificial load, to prove it can carry its rated load?
What is the inverter function called that stops a grid-tied PV system feeding the grid when the grid supply fails?
What is the set time after handover called, during which the contractor must put right any defects that appear?
What is the document called, signed by the client, that records the date they took over the finished installation? (two or three words)
What are the drawings called that are updated to show the installation exactly as it was finally installed?
What is the manual called that tells the client how to run and look after the installed systems? (words or letters)
A team must commission 18 motor circuits, and each one takes 40 minutes. How many hours of work is that?
Which instrument shows whether the three phases of a new supply are in the right order (L1, L2, L3)?
Which camera is used on a board under load to find joints that are running hot?
What is the UPS test called in which the load runs on the batteries alone for the specified time?
What is the stage called when the dead checks and tests are done, before a system is first energised?

essays.stem: You are the commissioning manager for the electrical services of a new small factory in Spanish Town. Describe what your commissioning plan would contain and how you would prepare it.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start from the contract, the specification and the drawings, and list every system to be commissioned: the main board, the sub-boards, the final circuits, the motors, the standby generator and its transfer switch, the emergency lighting and the fire alarm interface. For each I would set out the sequence: inspection and dead tests first, then energising from the supply outward, then the functional and performance tests. I would name the roles: the authorised person who energises, the testers, the recorders, the client's engineer who witnesses, and the makers' engineers. I would add an inspection and test plan showing each test, its accepted result, and the hold and witness points. I would list the instruments and check their calibration, and attach blank test sheets. Finally I would fit the plan into the programme, agree shutdowns and access with the client, and plan the handover documents and staff training.
markingPoints: Lists the systems in scope from the specification and drawings
Gives a clear sequence: dead tests, energising from the supply outward, then functional tests
Names the roles, including who energises and who witnesses
Includes test criteria, hold and witness points, records and calibrated instruments
Fits commissioning into the programme and plans handover and training

essays.stem: Explain the difference between pre-commissioning and commissioning. Give at least two examples of checks from each stage.
essays.modelAnswer: Pre-commissioning is the stage done with the installation dead, to prove it is complete, correct and safe to energise. Examples are the visual inspection of boards and terminations, checking that labels and covers are in place, and the dead tests: continuity of protective conductors, insulation resistance and polarity. Torque checks on large lugs and checking that the overload relays are set to the motor nameplate also belong here. Commissioning comes after, with the supply on. It proves that the systems work as the design intends. Examples are energising each board in turn, measuring voltages and phase rotation, live tests such as earth fault loop impedance and RCD trip times by a competent person, and functional tests such as starting motors, transferring to the generator, and running the emergency lighting on battery. Pre-commissioning must pass first, because energising a faulty installation could injure people or damage equipment.
markingPoints: Pre-commissioning is done dead to prove the installation is safe to energise
At least two correct pre-commissioning examples (inspection, continuity, insulation, polarity, settings)
Commissioning is done with power on to prove the systems work as designed
At least two correct commissioning examples (voltages, rotation, live tests, functional tests)
Explains why pre-commissioning must pass before energising

essays.stem: Describe the safe sequence for energising, for the first time, a new installation with a main board, two sub-boards and their final circuits. Say what controls you would put in place at each step.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would confirm that every inspection and dead test record is complete and signed, and that the government inspection has been passed and the supply connected. I would brief everyone on site, put up live warning notices and barriers, and mark the energisation drawing. With all outgoing ways off, the authorised person closes the main incoming breaker. We check the voltages and phase rotation at the main board. Next, the outgoing way to sub-board 1 is closed, with all of that board's ways off, and the voltages are checked there. The same is done for sub-board 2. Then the final circuits are switched on one at a time, checking each for correct operation and recording the readings. Any circuit not ready stays off, locked and tagged. After each step the drawing is updated so everyone knows what is live, and any later work on live parts goes under a permit to work.
markingPoints: Confirms dead test records, inspection and supply connection are complete first
Briefs people and uses notices, barriers and a live-status drawing
Energises from the supply outward with outgoing ways off at each board
Checks voltages and phase rotation at each board before going further
Keeps unready circuits locked off and uses a permit to work for later work

essays.stem: Explain how you would coordinate the commissioning of a new standby generator with an automatic transfer switch at a clinic in May Pen. Include the tests and the records.
essays.modelAnswer: I would agree a date with the clinic, because the tests cut the mains for short periods, and arrange for the maker's engineer to attend. Before any running, I would check that the generator's installation, fuel, exhaust, earthing and cabling are inspected and dead tested. With the maker's engineer, the generator is started off load and its voltage and frequency (50 Hz) are checked. A load bank test then proves it carries its rated load steadily for the time the specification gives. For the transfer switch, the authorised person opens the mains incoming breaker to simulate a failure. We time how long the generator takes to start and pick up the load. When the mains is restored, we check the delay before the load returns to mains and the generator's cool-down run. Each reading, time and setting is written on the test sheet, with the instrument used, and signed by the witnesses.
markingPoints: Plans the date with the client and involves the maker's engineer
Checks the installation is inspected and dead tested first
Checks voltage and 50 Hz frequency and carries out a load bank test
Simulates mains failure safely and times transfer, retransfer and cool-down
Records readings, times, settings and signatures

essays.stem: During a witnessed test at a hotel, the fire alarm interface fails to shut down one air handling unit. Explain how you would handle this, from the failure to closing it out.
essays.modelAnswer: I would stop that test, make the plant safe and record the failure on the test sheet straight away, with the time, what happened and who saw it. I would raise a non-conformance report so it is tracked. Then the cause must be found. That is done with the circuit isolated and locked off where wiring has to be checked. It may be a wrong terminal in the interface relay, a broken control cable or a setting in the air handling unit's controller. Once the cause is fixed, the related dead checks are repeated. I would then agree a new time with the client's engineer and the fire alarm contractor to repeat the full test with them present, not just the one unit, in case the repair affected others. When the retest passes, I record it, sign off the NCR, update the drawings if any wiring changed, and remove the item from the snag list.
markingPoints: Stops, makes safe and records the failure honestly at once
Raises a non-conformance report to track it
Finds the cause safely, with isolation for any wiring checks
Repeats the test with the witnesses present
Records the retest, closes the NCR and updates drawings or the snag list

essays.stem: Explain what hold points and witness points are in an inspection and test plan. Give an example of each on an electrical job and say why they matter.
essays.modelAnswer: An inspection and test plan lists each check and test, who does it, and the accepted result. A hold point is a step where work must stop until a named person, often the client's engineer, inspects it and releases it in writing. An example is cables in a trench: they must be inspected before the trench is backfilled, because once covered they cannot be checked. Another is the first energising of the main board. A witness point is a step where the named person is told in good time and may come to watch; if they do not come, the work can go on and the results are sent to them. An example is the insulation resistance test of a sub-main. These points matter because they give the client confidence, stop hidden work being covered before it is checked, and give a clear record of who saw what and when.
markingPoints: Hold point: work stops until the named person releases it
Correct electrical example of a hold point
Witness point: person is notified and may attend; work may go on if they do not
Correct electrical example of a witness point
Explains why they matter (confidence, hidden work, records)

essays.stem: Describe the documents you would put in the handover pack for a new commercial installation, and say why each one is needed.
essays.modelAnswer: The pack starts with the electrical installation certificate and the schedules of inspection and test results, which show the work was tested and met the specification. The government inspection certificate shows it was approved for connection. The commissioning sheets for each system, such as the generator, transfer switch, emergency lighting and motors, prove each one works and record the settings. As-built drawings and circuit charts show what is really installed, so later work can be done safely. The operation and maintenance manual explains how to run and look after each system, with the makers' data sheets, warranties and spare parts lists. A record of the client's staff training shows who was taught. The snag list with agreed dates shows what is still outstanding. Finally, a signed handover certificate records the date the client took over, which starts the defects liability period.
markingPoints: Certificate and test schedules, and the government inspection certificate
Commissioning sheets with settings for each system
As-built drawings and circuit charts
O&M manual with data sheets, warranties and spares
Training record, agreed snag list and signed handover certificate

essays.stem: Explain how you would coordinate and communicate with the people involved in commissioning a new mall in Montego Bay: the client, your own team, the makers' engineers, the other trades, the power company and the government inspector.
essays.modelAnswer: I would give everyone the commissioning programme early and keep it up to date. The client's engineer needs notice of every witness and hold point, and of any shutdown, so they can plan their staff and tenants. My own team gets a daily briefing on the tests, the roles and the safety controls, with the live-status drawing updated after each energising step. Makers' engineers for the generator, UPS and drives must be booked weeks ahead, with the site ready when they arrive. The other trades need to know which areas will become live, so they stop work there or work under control. The government inspector is booked when the installation is complete and tested, and the power company is given the certificate and paperwork they need before connection. I would keep minutes of the meetings and confirm decisions in writing, so everyone works from the same information.
markingPoints: Shares and updates a commissioning programme
Gives the client notice of witness points and shutdowns
Briefs own team daily, with safety controls and live-status information
Books makers' engineers and warns other trades of live areas
Arranges the inspection and power company connection, and confirms decisions in writing

essays.stem: Describe the checks and measurements you would make after a new installation is first energised and then put on load, and what you would do with the results.
essays.modelAnswer: Straight after energising, the voltages at each board are measured line to line and line to neutral, and the phase rotation is checked before any three-phase motor is run. A competent person carries out the live tests, such as earth fault loop impedance, prospective fault current and RCD trip tests, and each RCD's test button is tried. Each motor's rotation is checked with a brief start. Once the building is on load, the current in each phase of the sub-mains is measured with a clamp meter to see if the loads are balanced. After some hours on load, a thermal imaging survey of the boards finds any hot joints. I would compare every result with the design and the specification. Readings outside the limits go on an NCR or the snag list for action, and loads may be moved to balance the phases. All the readings are recorded so they can be compared at later inspections.
markingPoints: Measures voltages and checks phase rotation at each board
Live tests by a competent person and RCD test buttons tried
Measures phase currents on load to check balance
Thermal survey after some hours on load
Compares results with the design, records them and acts on faults

essays.stem: Explain how you would train the client's maintenance staff when you hand over a new installation with a generator and several distribution boards, and why this training matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I would agree with the client who will be trained and plan short sessions at the equipment, not only in a classroom. I would walk them round each board and show the circuit charts and labels, how to isolate and lock off a circuit, and how to prove dead with a tester checked before and after use. I would show how the generator and transfer switch work, how to read its alarms, and the routine checks the maker asks for, such as fuel and battery checks and a regular test run. I would show them how to use the RCD test buttons and the emergency lighting test. I would go through the O&M manual so they know where to find information and who to call. At the end I would record who was trained and on what. This matters because staff who understand the system can run it safely, spot problems early and avoid damage or injury.
markingPoints: Plans the training at the equipment with the right people
Covers isolation, lock-off and proving dead
Covers the generator, transfer switch and routine checks
Uses the O&M manual and keeps a training record
Explains why training matters (safety, early fault finding, care of equipment)

practical1.title: Pre-commissioning checks and an energisation plan for a training installation
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a training installation that is NOT connected to any supply: a small main board feeding a sub-board, a lighting circuit, an outlet circuit with an RCD (GFCI), a motor with a direct-on-line starter and overload relay, and an emergency light fitting. The assessor has planted some faults, such as a missing label, a loose terminal, an overload set wrongly and a missing cover. As a group, give each member a role (commissioning lead, two inspectors and testers, recorder, and safety lead), and swap so that everyone tests. Isolate and lock off the supply point with every member's padlock and a tag, and prove dead with a tester checked before and after use. Write a short inspection and test plan with hold and witness points. Carry out the pre-commissioning checks and dead tests, and record the readings. Set the overload to the motor's nameplate current. Write a snag list and an NCR for each fault, then a step-by-step energisation sequence for the instructor. If the Centre's rules allow, the instructor then energises the installation and runs the functional tests while the group stands behind the barrier and records what is witnessed; otherwise the assessor hands out a results sheet to record.
materials: Training installation (main board, sub-board, lighting, outlet with RCD/GFCI, motor and starter, emergency light) with planted faults, not connected to any supply
Lock-off kit with a multi-lock hasp, one padlock per member, and tags
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit
Screwdrivers, torch and a torque screwdriver
Blank ITP, test sheets, snag list and NCR forms
Barrier tape and live warning notices
Functional test results sheet (from the assessor, if the installation is not energised)
photos: The written ITP with hold and witness points marked
The supply point locked off with every member's padlock and a tag
The tester being checked on the proving unit before and after proving dead
Each planted fault with a label showing the group's finding
The overload relay set to the motor's nameplate current
The completed test sheets, snag list and NCRs
The energisation sequence, and the barrier set up for the instructor's energising
checklist: Took part in planning and wrote part of the ITP
Isolated, locked off and proved dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
Carried out at least one inspection check and one dead test correctly
Found and recorded faults on the snag list or an NCR
Set the overload relay correctly from the nameplate
Helped write a safe energisation sequence from the supply outward
Stayed behind the barrier and recorded witnessed results accurately
Left the installation, tools and paperwork safe and tidy
safety: The installation stays dead and locked off during all checks and tests; only the instructor energises anything
Every member fits their own padlock before any cover is opened
Warn others before each insulation test and let the circuit discharge before touching it
Keep behind the barrier while the instructor energises or runs the motor; guards stay fitted

practical2.title: Review commissioning results, close out failures and compile a handover pack
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a commissioning pack for a made-up small hotel in Ocho Rios: the drawings, the specification's acceptance limits, the dead test results, and a sheet of live and functional results (voltages, phase rotation, loop impedances, RCD trip times, generator start and transfer times, emergency lighting duration, fire alarm interface results and phase currents on load). Some results fail the specification. As a group, give each member a role (commissioning manager, results checker, NCR writer, document controller, and client trainer) and swap so everyone checks results. Check every result against the limits and mark it pass or fail. Raise an NCR for each failure, saying the likely cause and the action and retest needed. Work out the phase current balance from the figures. Build an index for the handover pack and list what is missing. Then role-play a handover meeting with the assessor as the hotel's engineer: present the open items, agree dates, and give a short training talk on isolating a circuit safely.
materials: Commissioning pack for a made-up hotel (drawings, specification limits, dead and live results sheets)
Blank NCR forms, snag list and handover pack index
Flip chart or whiteboard for the handover meeting
A sample O&M manual and sample as-built drawing
photos: The results sheets with each result marked pass or fail
The completed NCRs for each failed result
The handover pack index with missing items listed
The handover meeting role play, with the open items on the flip chart
The short training talk on isolation
checklist: Checked results against the specification limits correctly
Wrote at least one clear NCR with a cause, action and retest
Worked out the phase balance correctly
Helped build the handover pack index and found what was missing
Spoke clearly and accurately in the handover meeting
Gave or supported a correct explanation of safe isolation
Kept the records neat, dated and signed
safety: This is a desk and role-play task: no equipment is opened or energised
The training talk must teach switch off, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after
Treat the made-up client's information as confidential, as you would on a real job
